title: A Material Lens on Coloniality in NLP

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting and analyzing author institutional affiliations from 58,000 *CL papers to measure the geographic representation of researchers across different phases of the NLP pipeline (data production, annotation, modeling, deployment) and analyzing geographic disparities in hardware (GPU) usage.

Searching the plain text of NLP papers for mentions of specific languages, filtering the results using an LLM, and calculating linguistic diversity and equitability indices (Shannon Equitability Index and Gini Coefficient) over time to measure the dominance of Western European languages.

Conducting a case study on multilingual benchmarks (e.g., XQuaD) by categorizing the geographic and cultural focus of the underlying test set source material (e.g., Wikipedia articles) to demonstrate an English-centric, Western bias in cross-lingual evaluation.
Performing a qualitative case study on the systemic disparities, lack of representative datasets, and annotation biases affecting African American Vernacular English (AAVE) in NLP research.
